notes: Preliminary finite production episodes, not the full 25-minute/five-repetition Table 1 protocol.
The sustained episode permits eight minutes after the scheduled request; the short episode permits one minute. Input stops at the declared boundary in both cases, without a background low-rate phase.
The first 60 seconds are excluded from the admission cohort but deliberately develop the same backlog before evaluation; no stationary warm-up claim is made.
Two pairs per duration with reversed treatment order across pairs. Workload parameters and seed match within each pair; actual admissions and assignments remain measured.
The existing HPA remains paused. Scheduled 3-to-6 scaling is an action test, not a new selector or tuned HPA baseline.
The 60-second guard grace permits expected monitoring interruption after a scale request; missing observations still reduce analysis coverage and never count as recovery.
Retain unfavorable valid results. Stop for evidence/control problems and report technical exclusions explicitly.
Resource comparisons use common evaluation-through-drain horizons; calibration/setup is reported separately.
Recovery not confirmed during production is censored; do not substitute drain recovery for in-production recovery.
No confidence interval, universal superiority, novelty or legal eligibility claim follows from these short repeated pilots.
Revision 2 changes observation freshness to consumer monotonic age plus Prometheus sample age. Workload, timing, seeds, treatment order, freshness limit and live stop limits are unchanged.
The first revision-2 scale trial is also the live validation of this measurement repair. If the guard stops it, inspect and retain the diagnostic before further trials.

Completed evidence-valid trials remain in message-outcome comparisons even if monitoring coverage is low. Backlog and requested-resource comparisons each apply their predeclared coverage thresholds separately. Expected ownership gaps may reduce short-trial backlog coverage below 90 percent; they do not erase message outcomes.

The sequence pauses for runtime/evidence failure or achieved admission below 98 percent, and records low monitoring coverage for per-metric screening. It does not automatically stop the campaign solely for low lag coverage.

Revision 3 corrects the query union and checks actual complete fresh Prometheus partition observations before production release. Consumer application code, workload, timing, seeds, treatment order and guard thresholds are unchanged from revision 2.

The corrected query helper has been exercised against actual retained Prometheus data: all 60 owned partitions include both required age fields and pass the shared freshness predicate. This pre-release check is also repeated for every managed trial.

Revision 4 explicitly separates exporter schema/scrape readiness from valid Kafka position observations. An empty-topic unknown position passes startup only with explicit invalid/NaN lag and age fields, absent high/position gauges and a fresh original scrape timestamp. The manifest records valid versus unresolved counts. No unresolved lag is invented or included in analysis.

The complete production validity rule, 60-second warm-up, ten-second invalid-monitoring guard, action transition grace, workload, seeds, treatment order and timing are unchanged. Consumer application source remains unchanged from revision 2.
Both the full active-observation rule and the empty-topic schema readiness rule have been checked against actual retained Prometheus responses, in addition to 88 passing tests.
